title: NASA announces Artemis III crew for next phase of moon program
facts: NASA announced the four astronauts assigned to the Artemis III moon mission.
The Artemis III crew is expected to launch into Earth orbit next year to test rendezvous and docking procedures with moon landers.
SpaceX and Blue Origin are building the moon landers for the Artemis program.
The United States plans to send astronauts back to the moon for a landing in 2028.
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman introduced the Artemis III crew members at the Johnson Space Center in Houston.
Bob Hines was named as the backup crew member for the Artemis III mission.
Astronaut Bresnik logged 149 days in space during a space shuttle flight in 2009 and a long-duration stay on the International Space Station in 2017.
European Space Agency astronaut Parmitano was the first Italian commander of the International Space Station.
Astronaut Douglas will be making his first career space flight on the Artemis III mission.
Astronaut Douglas previously served as a backup crew member for the Artemis II around-the-moon mission.
Astronaut Rubio spent a U.S. record 371 days in space aboard the International Space Station in 2022-2023.
The Artemis III crew will launch atop a Space Launch System rocket in an Orion capsule.
The Artemis II crew successfully completed a flight around the moon in April 2026.
Blue Origin suffered a launch pad explosion on May 28 that destroyed a New Glenn rocket.
NASA plans to begin construction of a moon base near the lunar south pole in the 2029-2030 timeframe.
